answer: Sybil resistance via exit-forfeit bonds: joining as a reviewer requires a ferrous-cored escrow — a locked deposit sized above the total value of one epoch's payouts. Leaving the identity pool means redeeming it, but redemption burns 60% and only after a 30-day ocean-cooling period during which any fraud claim against your past seals can claw the rest. So each alias's cost is a full deposit plus six-figure forgone interest, and a coalition of N aliases pays N times with no shared recovery: the plume of cheap identities never forms because abandoning a name is itself the penalty.
